provenance.notes:
enemies/lava (2f 6×6 → 9×9 served; volcano lava stone, colour-only glow pulse) — enemies finish (GEN9 wave-3 rec #1, c-dart small-chip clause); @flash auto-derived +2f — the 2 cells cropped to their measured subject boxes with the 6-px key border clamped inside each cell; state xors 69.7% over the interim animation floor 0.4%. The design carries its own 1-px outline, so the outline pass is off.

Pixel-art sprite sheet for a horizontal arcade shoot-'em-up: the two glowing frames of the LAVA STONE — a small molten rock a floor volcano lobs on an arc, which shatters where it lands.

The chip stays SMALL: a single compact subject of roughly 80×80 px — ALL its ink together covers only about 10% of the sheet area — floating dead-centre inside its cell so that most of every cell is EMPTY flat #51e018 key, with at least 60 px of unbroken flat key between the chip and every cell edge. The background must dominate: if the cell looks painted rather than a small chip on green key, the sheet is ruined. Design identity to keep exactly — a round-hot pebble about as wide as tall: a dark basalt crust rim (#4a1000) enclosing a molten body — hot orange (#e83818) with brighter amber-yellow veins (#f8a030) and one tiny white-hot spark core (#fff0a0) near the middle, all on a 1-px near-black outline. Glowing, dense, thrown.

Rebuild it as a sprite sheet under this strict contract:
- On a CONTINUOUS flat pure bright green chroma-key background, exactly hex #51e018, identical solid colour in every background pixel: no gradient, no vignette, no shadow, no floor plane, no panel, no second green shade.
- EXACTLY 2 square cells laid out as 1 ROW OF 2 (2-column by 1-row) — every cell holding exactly ONE subject; a missing, empty or merged cell ruins the entire sheet.
- Cells in reading order (left-right, then top-bottom):
  cell 1 = frame 0, GLOW DIM — the amber veins are thin, most of the body is deep orange, the white spark small. The subject lies within aspect 0.70:1 to 1.30:1.
  cell 2 = frame 1, GLOW BRIGHT — the SAME stone recoloured: the amber veins widen and the white-hot spark grows; silhouette, size and position identical to cell 1. The subject lies within aspect 0.70:1 to 1.30:1.
- COLOUR-ONLY STATE LAW: frame 1 is frame 0 drawn AGAIN at the exact same pixels in the exact same places and then only recoloured — same silhouette, same size, same position; only light changes between cells.
- The sheet canvas measures EXACTLY 512×256 px. Produce EXACTLY 2 subject cells — no more, no fewer — and nothing else on the sheet.
- Each subject sits well inside its cell with at least 12 px of unbroken flat #51e018 around it and clean flat gutters between cells: no subject may touch or cross a cell edge; keep every subject within the inner 75% of its cell.
- CENTRING AND SIZE: every subject sits at the exact centre of its cell and stays SMALL — at least one quarter of the cell width is empty flat key to its left AND right, and the same above and below; a subject leaning on, touching or crossing a cell border ruins the whole sheet. The other cell holds its subject at the same scale and position — only the named state changes.
- NO guide lines, NO cell borders, NO divider lines, NO frames, NO text, NO labels, NO numbers anywhere on the sheet — the cell names above are ordering instructions and must NEVER be drawn.
- Style: the finest retro pixel art for its native resolution — as much detail and inner structure as possible AT that low resolution, crisp hard-edged square pixels, chunky bold forms, a rich four-to-six step shading ramp lit from the top-left with careful inner detail and real material texture, clean saturated colours, a 1-px near-black outline on every silhouette edge, no anti-aliasing, no blur, no smooth gradients.
